label: Job offer
text:
NORTHFIELD ANALYTICS, INC.
1200 Commerce Way, Floor 6
Wilmington, DE 19801

October 9, 2026

Dear Sam Okafor,

We are pleased to offer you the position of Senior Operations Analyst at Northfield Analytics, Inc. (the "Company"). This letter and the attached Employee Confidentiality, Invention Assignment and Restrictive Covenant Agreement (the "Covenant Agreement") set out the terms of your employment.

1. Position and Start Date. You will report to the Director of Revenue Operations. Your anticipated start date is November 16, 2026. This offer is contingent on the satisfactory completion of a background check and your proof of eligibility to work in the United States.

2. Work Location. This is a hybrid role. You will be expected to work from the Company's Wilmington office at least three (3) days per week. The Company may change the number of required in-office days, or your assigned office, at its discretion.

3. Base Salary. Your starting base salary will be $96,000.00 per year, paid in accordance with the Company's regular payroll schedule and subject to applicable withholdings. The Company may adjust your title, duties, reporting line, and compensation from time to time in its discretion.

4. Annual Bonus. You will be eligible for an annual performance bonus with a target of ten percent (10%) of your base salary. Whether any bonus is paid, and its amount, will be determined by the Company in its sole discretion based on individual and Company performance. You must be employed by the Company on the date bonuses are paid to receive any bonus for the prior year.

5. Signing Bonus. You will receive a one-time signing bonus of $10,000.00, less applicable withholdings, payable with your first regular paycheck. If your employment ends for any reason, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, within twenty-four (24) months of your start date, you agree to repay the full gross amount of the signing bonus within thirty (30) days of your last day of employment, and you authorize the Company to deduct any unpaid amount from your final paycheck to the extent permitted by law.

6. Equity. Subject to approval by the Company's Board of Directors, you will be granted an option to purchase 4,000 shares of the Company's common stock. The option will vest over four (4) years, with twenty-five percent (25%) vesting on the first anniversary of your start date and the remainder vesting in equal monthly installments over the following thirty-six (36) months, subject to your continued employment. The exercise price will be set by the Board on the date of grant. Any vested options must be exercised within thirty (30) days after your employment ends or they will be forfeited.

7. Benefits. You will be eligible to participate in the Company's medical, dental, and vision plans beginning on the first day of the month following sixty (60) days of employment, and in the Company's 401(k) plan after six (6) months of employment. The Company may modify or terminate any benefit plan at any time.

8. Paid Time Off. The Company offers a flexible paid time off policy. Time off must be approved in advance by your manager. Because time off under this policy does not accrue, no payment for unused time off will be made at the end of your employment.

9. Introductory Period. Your first ninety (90) days of employment will be an introductory period. During this period, you will not be eligible for severance under any Company plan or policy.

10. At-Will Employment. Your employment with the Company is at-will. Either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice. Nothing in this letter creates a contract of employment for any specific period.

11. Covenant Agreement. As a condition of employment, you must sign the Covenant Agreement. Key terms include:

(a) Non-Competition. During your employment and for eighteen (18) months after it ends for any reason, you will not, anywhere in the United States, perform services of any kind for any business that competes with the Company or that is developing products or services that would compete with the Company.

(b) Non-Solicitation. During your employment and for twenty-four (24) months after it ends, you will not solicit or accept business from any customer or prospective customer of the Company, and you will not solicit or hire any Company employee or contractor.

(c) Invention Assignment. You assign to the Company all inventions, works of authorship, software, ideas, and other intellectual property that you conceive or develop during your employment, whether or not during working hours, whether or not using Company equipment or information, and whether or not related to the Company's business.

(d) Confidentiality. You will not use or disclose the Company's confidential information during or after your employment.

(e) Remedies. If you breach the Covenant Agreement, the restricted periods will be extended by the length of the breach, and you will pay the Company's attorney's fees and costs of enforcement.

12. Dispute Resolution. Any dispute arising out of your employment, including claims under federal, state, or local law, will be resolved exclusively by final and binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware, on an individual basis. You waive any right to bring or participate in a class or collective action. Each party will bear its own attorney's fees, except as provided in the Covenant Agreement.

13. Outside Activities. While employed, you may not engage in any other employment, consulting, or business activity without the prior written approval of the Company.

14. Expiration. This offer will expire if not signed and returned by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 14, 2026.

We are excited about the prospect of you joining the team.

Sincerely,

Renee Castillo
Vice President, People Operations
Northfield Analytics, Inc.

ACCEPTED AND AGREED:

Sam Okafor

Date: ______________

reading.title: Offer letter for Senior Operations Analyst at Northfield Analytics
reading.summary: This is a job offer from Northfield Analytics, Inc. to Sam Okafor for a hybrid Senior Operations Analyst role. It pays $96,000.00 a year, with a 10% target bonus, a $10,000.00 signing bonus, and 4,000 stock options. The biggest issue is the attached Covenant Agreement. It bars you from working for any competitor anywhere in the United States for 18 months after you leave, and it claims everything you create while employed, even on your own time. The offer expires today, October 14, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

push_back.title: Nationwide non-compete on any work
push_back.why: A non-compete is a promise not to work for competitors after you leave. This one covers the whole country, lasts 18 months, applies even if you are fired, and bans services of any kind, not only similar roles.
push_back.ask: Can you limit the non-compete to roles like mine, at direct competitors, in a smaller area, for 6 months, and drop it if I am let go without cause?
push_back.quote: for eighteen (18) months after it ends for any reason, you will not, anywhere in the United States, perform services of any kind for any business that competes with the Company

push_back.title: Full bonus payback even if fired
push_back.why: You owe back the whole $10,000.00 gross, which is more than you received after taxes, even if the Company lets you go. There is no reduction for time served.
push_back.ask: Can repayment apply only if I quit or am fired for cause, and shrink month by month over 12 months?
push_back.quote: If your employment ends for any reason, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, within twenty-four (24) months of your start date, you agree to repay the full gross amount of the signing bonus

push_back.title: Company owns your side projects
push_back.why: The Company claims anything you create while employed, even on your own time, with your own equipment, and unrelated to its business.
push_back.ask: Can you limit the assignment to work related to the Company's business or made with its resources, and let me list prior inventions I keep?
push_back.quote: whether or not during working hours, whether or not using Company equipment or information, and whether or not related to the Company's business

push_back.title: Short window to buy vested options
push_back.why: You get only 30 days after leaving to pay to buy your vested shares, or you lose them. That can mean a large cash outlay on short notice.
push_back.ask: Can the exercise window be extended to at least 90 days, or longer if I am let go without cause?
push_back.quote: Any vested options must be exercised within thirty (30) days after your employment ends or they will be forfeited.

push_back.title: One-sided legal fees
push_back.why: You pay the Company's lawyers if it enforces the Covenant Agreement, but the Company has no matching duty. The restrictions can also run longer than stated.
push_back.ask: Can the fee clause apply to whichever side wins, and can you remove the automatic extension of the restricted periods?
push_back.quote: the restricted periods will be extended by the length of the breach, and you will pay the Company's attorney's fees and costs of enforcement.

good_to_know.title: Arbitration and no class actions
good_to_know.why: Arbitration means a private arbitrator decides disputes instead of a court. You also give up joining group lawsuits.
good_to_know.quote: will be resolved exclusively by final and binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware, on an individual basis. You waive any right to bring or participate in a class or collective action.

good_to_know.title: Bonus requires being on payroll
good_to_know.why: If you leave or are let go before bonuses are paid, you get nothing for the prior year, even if you earned it.
good_to_know.quote: You must be employed by the Company on the date bonuses are paid to receive any bonus for the prior year.

good_to_know.title: No payout for unused time off
good_to_know.why: Flexible PTO has no balance, so nothing is paid out when you leave.
good_to_know.quote: Because time off under this policy does not accrue, no payment for unused time off will be made at the end of your employment.

good_to_know.title: Company can change pay and role
good_to_know.why: Your title, duties, and pay can be changed later at the Company's discretion. The in-office days and office location can change too.
good_to_know.quote: The Company may adjust your title, duties, reporting line, and compensation from time to time in its discretion.

good_to_know.title: Customers and coworkers are off limits
good_to_know.why: For 24 months you cannot take business from customers even if they come to you, and you cannot hire Company staff.
good_to_know.quote: you will not solicit or accept business from any customer or prospective customer of the Company, and you will not solicit or hire any Company employee or contractor.

good_to_know.title: No side work without approval
good_to_know.why: Any freelancing, consulting, or side business needs written sign-off first.
good_to_know.quote: you may not engage in any other employment, consulting, or business activity without the prior written approval of the Company.

before_you_sign: Ask for a short extension, since the offer expires today at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.
Get the full Covenant Agreement and read it, because this letter only summarizes it.
Check the rules where you live on non-competes and invention assignments.
Write down any inventions or side projects you already own and ask to attach the list.
Get any agreed changes in writing in a revised letter before you sign.
Consider a short review by an employment lawyer given the non-compete.

email.subject: Questions on Senior Operations Analyst offer
email.body:
Hi Renee,

Thank you for the offer. I am excited about the role and have a few questions before I sign. Given that the offer expires today, could you extend the deadline by a few days so we can sort these out?

1. Could the non-compete be limited to roles like mine at direct competitors, a smaller area, and 6 months, and not apply if I am let go without cause?
2. Could the signing bonus repayment apply only if I resign or am fired for cause, and reduce month by month?
3. Could the invention assignment cover only work related to the Company's business or made with Company resources, with a list of my prior inventions excluded?
4. Could the window to exercise vested options be extended to at least 90 days?
5. Could the attorney's fees clause apply to whichever side wins, and could the automatic extension of the restricted periods be removed?
6. Could you send me the full Covenant Agreement to review?

Thank you for your help.

[Your name]
